entries.3d833068d913c6e8: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥2,311,267 million, up 8.5% from the previous year. Revenue from external customers was ¥682,812 million for Power Sports & Engine, the largest, followed by ¥613,691 million for Aerospace Systems, ¥433,574 million for Energy Solutions & Marine, ¥259,146 million for Precision Machinery & Robotics, ¥236,203 million for Rolling Stock and ¥85,839 million for Other. Only Other recorded a decline in revenue, while the other five recorded increases. The company cites as reasons for the increases: in Power Sports & Engine, higher four-wheel vehicle sales for North America and motorcycle sales for advanced countries; in Aerospace Systems, higher sales to the Ministry of Defense and shared-manufacture products for civil aircraft; in Energy Solutions & Marine, higher revenue in the ship and marine field and the plant field; in Precision Machinery & Robotics, strong hydraulic equipment sales for China's construction machinery market and higher sales of robots for semiconductor manufacturing equipment; and in Rolling Stock, higher sales to domestic and U.S. customers.

As concrete examples of the three fields the company focuses on, there are the surgical-support robot 'hinotori' (a cumulative total of 110 units installed in Japan and overseas as of the end of March 2026), a shipbuilding contract with Nihon Suiso Energy Co., Ltd. for a 40,000 m³-class liquefied hydrogen carrier (announced January 2026), the start of construction of the 'Kawasaki LH₂ Terminal' liquefied hydrogen base at Ōgishima in Kawasaki City (November 2025), and a demonstration facility for CO2 separation and recovery at the Kobe plant (completed November 2025).
